text:
anya: heads up — onboarding mamba-2.1 (q4f16) into staging. quick smoke shows a reproducible quality drop on our yue_subtitles testset :thinking:

kai: can you paste an example? is this detok or tokenization?

anya: short repro below — original line (Cantonese subtitle):
```
佢話：「我哋冇得揀」。
```
mamba-2.0 (fp16) output: `佢 話 ： 「 我哋 冇 得 揀 」 。`
mamba-2.1 q4f16 output: `佢話：「我哋冇得揀」。`
BLEU drop ~ 4.6 on the subset (mostly spacing/segmentation).

sophia: so the q4f16 model is joining graphemes back together? that looks like detokenization *improved* (no extra spaces) but BLEU went down — weird. do we have reference detok?

anya: baseline tokenization uses sentencepiece with surgery rules we apply for yue (we enforce inter-character spaces for our eval pipeline). mamba-2.1 seems to emit different token boundaries that our detok postproc doesn't expect. eval-bot: automatic regression flagged on 2026-03-19 08:34 UTC — metric delta: BLEU -4.6, chrF -2.1, token-coverage drop 0.9%.

kai: could this be caused by the new tokenizer merge table we applied during quantization conversion? iirc we run a vocab-prune step for q4f16 to remove rare pieces.

dylan: attached a small bisect script I ran locally that toggles the vocab-prune. reproducer:
```bash
# toggle vocab-prune and score on yue_subtitles 200-sample
python scripts/score_onset.py --model mamba-2.1 --quant q4f16 --prune-vocab True
python scripts/score_onset.py --model mamba-2.1 --quant q4f16 --prune-vocab False
```
results: prune=True -> BLEU 22.7, prune=False -> BLEU 27.3

sophia: huge. so pruning removed some multi-char pieces that were important for Cantonese segmentation. That explains boundary changes. Probably merged many |Han|Han| tokens into single nodes earlier/later.

anya: I inspected token ids around the phrase. with prune=True the segment sequence is shorter, and our yue detok expects per-char boundaries which we lose. sample token ids (prune True): `[..., 1045, 29827, 40221, ...]` (prune False): `[..., 1045, 1202, 1203, 1204, ...]`

kai: two possible mitigation paths:
1) revert prune for the yue evaluation variant and keep prune for general release (per-locale vocab overrides)
2) adjust postproc detok to tolerate merged tokens (but that might mask other regressions)

sophia: option 1 is safest for correctness. we should generate a per-locale vocab-exception list for CJK variants where we preserve pieces. produces no perf hit for most inputs if we scope it to named locales.

dylan: agree. i prototyped a fallback that expands merged tokens by mapping them back using the original sentencepiece NBest decode. it's messy and slower.

anya: for short term can we pin mamba-2.1-q4f16:prune-off for yue staging only? then run full eval across zh-hant/zh-hans/ja/ko to ensure no regressions.

kai: will add a rollout policy: route locale=yue AND dataset=subtitle -> mamba-2.1-q4f16:prune-off. I'll push config in infra.

eval-bot: scheduled eval: yue_subtitles (200) + zh_hant_news (500) + ja_dialog (300). expected to finish in ~45m.

sophia: long term we should add a vocab-delta test in our onboarding — compute tokenization stability per-language when pruning/merging. threshold e.g., >1% token coverage change -> fail bring-up.

anya: agreed. can someone open a quick RFC for per-locale vocab-exceptions + onboarding guardrails? I'll include the failing examples and bisect notes.

dylan: i'll draft RFC and add the script + small dataset. ping me for review @sophia

kai: config PR up in 10m. i'll coordinate rollout after eval finishes. :thumbsup:

sophia: thanks all. tl;dr — mamba-2.1 q4f16 vocab-prune caused Cantonese token merges -> BLEU regression on subtitles. short-term: route yue -> prune-off. long-term: vocab-exception lists + token-stability checks in onboarding.

anya: adding one more note: watch out for ZWJ/BRACKET interactions in yue — some merged tokens remove ZWJ and change rendering for karaoke lines. i added two examples to the RFC.

eval-bot: eval complete. results: yue_subtitles BLEU improved to baseline with prune-off, zh_hant and ja show no significant regressions.

anya: closing loop, moving PR to canary. thanks!
